mainEntity.name: How long does it take to get used to veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients find that the initial sensation of unfamiliarity or thickness resolves within one to two weeks. During this period, the tongue, lips, and bite gradually adapt to the new tooth surfaces. Speech may feel slightly different for the first few days, and some mild temperature sensitivity can occur. If sensations of thickness or discomfort persist beyond two to three weeks without improvement, it is advisable to contact your dental practice so that your team can review the fit and determine whether any adjustment is needed.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for veneers to feel bulky?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, feeling a sense of bulk or prominence after veneer placement is a very common experience. Even though veneers are extremely thin — typically between 0.3 mm and 0.7 mm — the mouth's sensory system is highly attuned to even the smallest changes. This means that perfectly fitted veneers can initially feel more prominent than they actually are. In the vast majority of cases, this sensation diminishes naturally over the adjustment period as the brain habituates to the new surfaces. It is important not to make final judgements about the fit in the first few days.

mainEntity.name: Can a dentist make veneers thinner after they have been fitted?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some cases, minor contouring or polishing can refine the feel or appearance of veneers after fitting. However, significant structural changes are limited once a veneer is bonded, as the material has a finite thickness. If there is a genuine concern about the overall size or thickness following the adjustment period, your dental team may assess whether adjustment, or in some instances replacement, is appropriate. This decision depends entirely on a clinical examination and cannot be determined without professional assessment.

Some patients notice a slight change in speech immediately after veneer placement, particularly when pronouncing sounds that involve the tongue touching the front teeth — such as 's', 't', or 'th' sounds. This is a temporary adjustment and usually resolves within a few days to a week as the tongue adapts. Practising speaking aloud at home can help speed up this process. If speech difficulties persist beyond a couple of weeks, it is worth mentioning to your dental team during a follow-up appointment.

Veneers do not require dramatically different maintenance from natural teeth, but certain considerations apply. A non-abrasive fluoride toothpaste is recommended to avoid scratching the veneer surface. Daily flossing remains essential to maintain gum health at the veneer margins. Avoiding biting very hard foods directly with veneered teeth is also advisable. For patients who grind their teeth, a night guard may be recommended by their dentist. Regular check-up and hygiene appointments are an important part of ongoing veneer care and should not be overlooked.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my veneer feels loose or has come off?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a veneer becomes loose or detaches, you should contact your dental practice as soon as possible to arrange an assessment. Do not attempt to reattach the veneer yourself using over-the-counter adhesives, as this can complicate professional rebonding. Keep the veneer safe and bring it with you to your appointment. Veneer debonding can occur for various reasons, including excessive bite force, trauma, or the natural ageing of the bonding material, and your dental team will advise on the most appropriate course of action following examination.
